This level is a very nice end to the 10's column. It is fun, hard, and entertaining. The two rockets provide good protection to the very open level, and there is plenty of room for playing around. From the start, run to the right, jump over the launchpad, then jump and walljump into the first crosshair. Dodge the rocket if it got in, then jump in, flip the switch, and drop out. Launch yourself up, walljump, and land in the top crosshair. Jump across, flip the switch, then drop through the top of the center. Activate the terminal, then drop on the bounceblock on the left, and continue down and to the left. Jump and walljump, and flip the third switch, to drop down. Launch and walljump, then jump across and flip the final switch, then jump up to the ledge, and run to the exit, beating the column.
Quote from the NEHS

Sixty nine squared = 692 = 4761 and sixty nine cubed = 693 = 328509. These two answers use all the digits from 0 to 9 between them.
You can chop a big lump of cheese into a maximum of 93 bits with 8 straight cuts
In the English language "forty" is the only number that has all its letters in alphabetical order.
1 37 = 0027027027... and 1 27 = 0037037037...
132 = 169 and if you write both numbers backwards you get 312 = 961.
This also works with 12 because 122 = 144 and 212 =441.
1/1089 = 000091827364554637281... (And the numbers in the 9 times table are 9,18,27,36...)
8 is the only cube that is 1 less than a square.

To record it...

1. get the data.
2. Load it or if you have it already, reset it.
3. Press 1, then P, then play the level.
4. Once you have finished press 2.
5. Copy it to where you want.


To test it...
1. Get the demo.
2. Press 3.
3. Then press Q, then P (make sure you have CAPS LOCK ON)
4. Finished.

#12996 1 2006-12-19T19:03:11Z 29403
The N Factor![/color]

The Rules[/color]
The rules are similar to SCD, and a bit like Changing Enemies by max_ride.
Basically, you have 17 days to make a very effortfull map. I will choose the style of map. After with our 4 judges we mark the map like this:
n/5 for tileset.
n/5 for playbility. {Except for Quick DDAs}
n/5 for effort.
n/5 for length.
n/5 for how fun it looks {Just for quick DDAs}
Half marks are given. You may explain why you gave it the mark!
Total score should be n/20.
If you come last with the judges you get just the one point. If your score is the highest you get the number of participants as your point. The rounds are as follows:
1. Action
2. Survival
3. Puzzles
4. Tileset {This is just marked overall out of 20}
5. Prisoner
6. Race
7. Quick DDAs As short as you like. Have a go! If you can't do it I'll double your score on the Race round.
You can also join in the middle of the contest. You will get your points timesd by the round number. So if you start making a quick DDa and get 8 points, you get your score timesd by 6 which makes 48. You can also drop out. If you drop out on prisoner, you double the score of the last round.
You can only submit one map per round
You can submit old maps.
This week it is Action - get mapmaking!

Prizes[/b]
1st Prize = 2 sig tags + 2 dedication tileset
2nd prize = 2 tags + 1 dedication tileset
3rd prize = 1 tag + 1 ded tileset
4th prize = 1 tag
5th Prize = 1 tag

Judges
Me
Hypnotizer
ChaseTheBase
numa_ninja

Round 1 Maps - Action Maps[/u]
1. max_ride - max_ride's map
2. rocket_thwumped - Absolut Zero
3. romainiac - Fly Away

That's the little gem I got this idea from.
Murderous Maths - the key to the universe

To find the remiender when dividing by 9 look at the numbers that repeat - that is the remainder.

e.g: 157/99 = 1.58585858585858... so the remiender is 58 (the 2 numbers after the decimal point) It also works for 999 - the first 3 after the . and also 9999 and so on!

Quote: McP3000, December 21, 2006 01:43 am
Whats a perfect number?
A perfect number is when all it's factors (except itself) added together make the number.

e.g. 6 = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6
28 = 1 + 2 + 4 + 7 + 14 = 28

#274929 11 2006-12-22T12:55:28Z 29403
Quote: LittleViking001, December 22, 2006 12:46 am
The most common cause of accidental NaNs is pressing L before clicking outside of the level data box. If the game generated a ! at the very end of the level data, the L at the end of the data would get discarded and there wouldn't be any NaN like there would be now. The same goes for the somewhat rare case of leaving a # at the end of level data and trying to load it. Normally it would produce a NaN, but with an exclamation point before it, N just throws it away.

Edit: See the example if you don't understand. Paste the data in N and press L without clicking out of the data box.

#13263 1 2007-01-01T17:14:37Z 29403
Your Underrated Maps

Just like the underrated map thread, you post maps that you think are underrated, but unlike the UMT, you can post only your maps. But...

1. Only post maps with a rating 3 or under
2. Do not post maps with less than 5 votes. Use the Map Rating/Commenting thread.
3. You can post as many maps as you like, but you can't be sure people will rate up them all
4. Rate what you think the map should get, not a 5.
5. You can't guarantee that your map is rated 3.5-5, if you think the above map deserves what it has don't rate it.
6. You can post your map twice only if still remains 3 or under.

While I like the program, I totally respect your opinion.
Many maps are getting overrated just because they use a player-mod. While a avereage map with a drone-mod may get a 4, a very well made map with no mod will get the same rating, even though it's better. Some people just use those mods just to get a higher bar graph over the 4.

I don't really think that people have left because of NReality. NReality covered a long time period, so it's obvious that some people would have left. It's got nothing to do with NReality, I mean, that's just ridiculous.

Yes, soon people will want a multiplayer option, and N will never be the same again. It will be a very complicated game and will lose all the simpleness that made N a great game.

Also, I fully agree with you on the player-mods. N should be left alone. N should never be changed in any level. It just complicates the game.

Unfortunately for you, Unreality is going to release a load of mods, so it won't die unless Unreality and the other members run out of ideas.

N is supposed to be simple game, not a game with lots of silly complex mods.

I respect your points. Yeah, everyone's going to bash you just because they love the program. But your points are valid.

There are some very well made levels made with NReality, made by incluye, Evil_Bob and Templex. They deserve good ratings. NReality has some of the ideas we suggested in N 1.5 which were implimented. It's a nice program to play with while we wait in vain for N 1.5. You don't have to submit the maps, you can play with the mods.

Yeah, I agree with Thomas. It's a little harsh that you want NReality to be forgotten. It's there to keep us busy while we wait for N 1.5. Why do you want to forget it?

Wow, a lot of editing and a superlong post! =)

It's your opinion, though. Not everyone can like NReality.
